docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
Documentation for Compiler’s analytics and business intelligence workspace.

This project provides the infrastructure and services for setting up Metabase and GCP resources.

docs.title: Key Architecture Decisions
docs.text: Component Selected Configuration Rationale GCP Project data-warehouse-492522 Host project containing BigQuery analytics warehouse and infrastructure. GCP Region us-west1 (Oregon) Optimal low-latency to California; standard Tier 1 GCP pricing (matches us-central1 costs). Domain & DNS dashboards.compiler.la (Cloudflare) Free managed SSL certificates; CNAME pointing to Cloud Run; proxy/WAF protection. Container Runtime GCP Cloud Run Zero Kubernetes overhead; fully managed container lifecycle; integrated Cloud SQL proxy; native HTTPS. Instance Policy Min Instances: 1 Prevents cold-start delays and ensures Metabase background syncs, alerts, and scheduled pulses run continuously. Application Database Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Production-ready state store for Metabase (dashboards, queries, users, permissions). Never use the default embedded H2 database in production. Analytics Warehouse Google BigQuery Native driver built into Metabase. Authenticated via the Cloud Run attached Service Account (no JSON key rotation needed). Authentication Dual Auth: Google OAuth + Password Google Workspace OAuth restricted to @compiler.la for internal staff, plus password invites enabled for external stakeholders. Outbound Email Google Workspace SMTP Relay Reliable delivery of user invitations, password resets, and automated dashboard subscriptions. Secrets Management GCP Secret Manager Securely injects database passwords, encryption keys, and client secrets directly into container environment variables. Data Orchestration Google Cloud Workflows Serverless orchestration for API and file ingestion. Low-cost and scales to zero. Data Modeling dbt Core Open-source analytics modeling; run as containerized jobs on Cloud Run to avoid dedicated VMs. Ingestion Method Python Scripts Leverage existing Python libraries (e.g., Toggl access) to land raw data into GCS.

docs.title: Production Cost Estimates
docs.text: This page provides an initial monthly pricing estimate for the production environment of the Dashboards project. These figures are based on minimal production-ready configurations and low request volumes.

docs.title: Monthly Estimated Cost Breakdown
docs.text: Resource Configuration Estimated Monthly Cost Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) 1 vCPU, 3.75 GB RAM, 100 GB SSD $60 - $90 Cloud Run (Metabase/dbt) Min instances = 1, Low volume $10 - $30 Cloud Workflows Serverless orchestration $1 - $5 BigQuery Minimal ingestion & storage $0 - $5 GCS Storage < 1 GB total $0 - $1 Total Estimated Monthly $71 - $131

docs.title: Key Assumptions & Notes
docs.text:
• Cloud SQL: Sized for a small team (approx. 20 users) to ensure smooth performance for Metabase metadata operations.
  • Cloud Run: Includes a minimum of 1 instance to eliminate “cold start” delays for users.
  • Cloud Workflows: Replaced Cloud Composer to provide a serverless, pay-per-execution model, significantly reducing the baseline infrastructure cost.
  • Data Costs: Based on current dataset sizes (~333 KB/month). Costs are expected to remain negligible until data volume scales significantly.
  • Variability: These are estimates. Actual costs may fluctuate based on specific usage patterns and GCP pricing updates in the us-west1 region.

docs.title: Helper Scripts
docs.text:
The following helper scripts are available to run inside the dev container:

  • Wait for Metabase to initialize:
./bin/wait-for-metabase.sh
  • Connect to the local Postgres metadata database:
./bin/psql.sh

docs.title: Getting Started with Dashboards
docs.text: This is a tutorial on how to set up your local development environment.

docs.title: Local Development (VS Code Dev Containers)
docs.text:
This repository follows Compiler’s cross-platform Dev Containers standard to ensure consistent development environments across macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Note

Read our blog post on Dev Containers to learn more about Compiler’s cross-platform development philosophy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Docker and Docker Compose running locally (check out Podman for a cross-platform OSS management environment).
  2. Visual Studio Code.
  3. VS Code Dev Containers Extension.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Copy the sample environment file:
cp .env.example .env
  1. Open this folder in VS Code.
  2. When prompted, click “Reopen in Container” (or press F1 / Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P and run Dev Containers: Reopen in Container).
  3. VS Code will build the dev container and launch all three services:
  4. dev: Your development shell containing terraform, gcloud, pre-commit, and Postgres client tools.
  5. postgres: Local PostgreSQL 16 database storing Metabase application state.
  6. metabase: Official Metabase application available at http://localhost:3000.
